entities.summary: Salvius, Salvi or Sauve, was a bishop of Albi in Francia between 574 and 584, later venerated as a saint in the Catholic Church. His feast day is 10 September. Salvius played a crucial role in the Merovingian dynasty's religious and political landscape. As bishop, he oversaw the construction of numerous churches, including the Basilica of Sainte-Cécile in Albi. Salvius's leadership and theological expertise earned him recognition by the Frankish king, Chilperic I, and his successor, Childebert II. The bishop's legacy extended beyond his own time, influencing the development of Christian doctrine and the establishment of the Albigensian heresy. Salvius's reputation as a saint has endured for centuries, with his feast day celebrated annually by Catholics around the world. The bishop's historical significance lies in his ability to navigate the complex web of power and religion in medieval Francia, a testament to his piety, intelligence, and diplomatic acumen.
